descriptionChirho: General interpersonal strife, dispute, or contention without specific juridical nuance; consistently Arabic khaasama (خَاصَمَ) and takhaasama (تَخَاصَمَ), Korean datuda (다투다), Swahili -shindana and -gombana, Hindi jhagdaa (झगड़ा) and ladaa (लड़ा).

Juridical advocacy, legal defense, or formal pleading of a case on behalf of oneself or another; distinguished by Arabic raafa'a (رَافَعَ) and da'waa (دَعْوَى), Korean byeonho (변호) and byeonnon (변론) meaning legal defense, Swahili -tetea (to defend/advocate), Hindi mukaddamaa (मुकदमा, lawsuit), and Spanish defender/abogar.

Hifil participial form denoting an adversary or antagonist, one who contends against another; Arabic mukhaasimuu (مُخَاصِمُو), Korean datuneun jadeul (다투는자들), Swahili adui (enemy) and wapinzani (opponents).

Causative stem occurrence rendered as setting an ambush or lying in wait, semantically distinct from all contention senses; Arabic kamana (كَمَنَ, to lurk), Korean maebok (매복, ambush), Swahili -shuka (descend/attack); likely a homographic or textual-critical variant.
Noun form riiv (רִיב) used substantively to denote a dispute, quarrel, or lawsuit; Arabic khusuuma (خُصومَة, litigation), Korean songsa (송사, lawsuit), Swahili ugomvi (quarrel/dispute).
